How it answers

Two tracks, and the machine decides which, not the customer.

A contractor should never have to work out whether his job is the simple kind. He describes it, and the equipment itself settles what happens next.

Instant Reserve

For machines a number can describe.

Dig depth, working height, transport width, operating weight. Those are figures off a spec sheet, not judgment calls. He says he needs three metres of depth behind a building with a 2.4 metre gate; the system matches it, checks what is actually free on those dates, and holds the unit. At ten at night, without waiting on anybody.

Quote Required

For anything that comes off a load chart.

Crane and rigging capacity changes with radius, so it is never priced automatically. Not by us, not by software, not ever. The job gets captured properly, weight, pick height, set height, radius, access, ground conditions, and lands with your estimator as a complete brief. He prices it. He just stops having to ring the customer back to find out what the job is.

That second paragraph is the part worth reading twice. Every owner in this business has been pitched software that claims it can quote a lift. We are telling you plainly that we refuse to, and why.

The part that outlasts us

Your fleet, written down properly, for the first time.

To match a job to a machine, the system has to hold real specifications as real data, not a brochure photo, not a scanned data plate, not a PDF. Once that exists, it pays a second time.

A page per class, on your domain

Generated from the fleet we build during setup. Not a website rebuild, we do not touch the site you already have.

Readable by a search engine

Specs as text a crawler can actually parse, rather than as a picture of a spec sheet that nothing can read.

Readable by an assistant

Contractors have started asking ChatGPT who rents a forty-ton rough terrain near them. Whoever's fleet is legible gets named. Most yards are a brochure.

Yours to keep

The fleet build, the rate cards, the pricing rules and the scripts. You are not renting them from us.

We will not promise you a ranking or a citation. We publish pages that can be read; what any search engine or assistant does with them is not ours to guarantee, and anybody who tells you otherwise is selling.

Day ninety

Nothing you paid for disappears.

The closers come off. The machine does not. That is the whole design, the ninety days exist to prove a number on your own yard, and the system is what makes the number repeatable once they are gone.

The honest version

Two doors, and we are happy with either.

Keep us managed and we keep working the pipeline. Or take the closers off and run the machine yourselves, with the reporting you have been reading every Monday still in front of you. Either way you keep everything we built. What that costs is a twenty-minute conversation, not a number on a web page.
